findings: All 31 Texas inventory routes are direct-gauge scored routes; no proxy or planning Texas routes remain.

Official TPWD/SARA/LCRA pages still support the Guadalupe Valley, Upper Guadalupe, San Antonio River Goliad, Village Creek, South Llano, Bastrop Wilbarger, Bastrop El Camino Real, Columbus, Brazos Columbia Bottomland, and Brazos Gulf Prairie route shapes, endpoint names, endpoint coordinates or access-address anchors, and practical safety caveats.
NPS still supports Village Creek access sequencing, year-round sandbar camping, low-water log/sandbar cautions, and high-water hazard warnings.

Camping classifications remain conservative: Guadalupe routes are none, Village Creek ranges from nearby_basecamp to endpoint_campground and overnight_capable, and South Llano ranges from endpoint_campground to on_route_campsite.
Gallery-image coverage now has either an approved reusable image or a documented bounded no-image row for every Texas route.

The later Colorado River Wilbarger, Bastrop El Camino Real, Columbus, Upper Guadalupe, Goliad, Brazos Columbia Bottomland, and Brazos Gulf Prairie adds are direct-USGS scored; the Bastrop gauge is currently above Wilbarger's conservative 200 cfs floor but below the downstream El Camino Real 800 cfs local floor, while Columbus, Upper Guadalupe, and Goliad are above their conservative floors, and Brazos is above its ideal band in a hazardous safety-cue range.

The Guadalupe River State Park-to-Nichol's Landing add is a direct-USGS scored Upper Guadalupe route-family card with TPWD endpoint/portage/private-bank evidence, TRPA two-sided thresholds, endpoint-campground classification, and a bounded no-image row.

The upper SASPAMCO River Crossing Park-to-Helton add is a direct-USGS scored San Antonio River route-family card with TPWD/SARA endpoint and closure-boundary evidence, TRPA minimum-only thresholds, Helton endpoint-campground classification, and a bounded no-image row.

The Buffalo Bayou Woodway-to-Sabine add is a direct-USGS scored urban route-family card with TPWD access/safety/water-quality evidence, Save Buffalo Bayou 150 cfs minimum-only flow support, no route camping, access-anchor coordinate offsets, generated geometry, and a bounded no-image row.

The Elm Fork Trinity LLELA-to-Hebron add is a direct-USGS scored National Water Trail route-family card with LLELA access/current-conditions/camping evidence, Trinity Coalition coordinates, LLELA 80-600 cfs guidance, endpoint-campground classification, generated geometry, and a bounded no-image row.

The West Fork Trinity Panther-Island-to-Handley-Ederville add is a direct-USGS scored National Water Trail route-family card with Trinity Coalition public launch coordinates, TRPA 100 cfs minimum-only support, no route camping, urban runoff/dam/strainer/muddy-bank safety notes, and a bounded no-image row.

The Dallas Trinity Trammell-Crow-to-Loop-12 add is a direct-USGS scored National Water Trail / TPWD route-family card with TPWD and Trinity Coalition public access coordinates, TRPA 100 cfs minimum-only support, no route camping, Dallas Wave scout/portage handling, urban water-quality and dam safety notes, generated geometry, coordinate review offsets, and a bounded no-image row.
conclusion: The prior Texas saturation decision is superseded by later bounded discovery route additions. Texas now has 31 scored direct-USGS routes and remains active for the next bounded discovery rotation.
